title: Contain and remediate inference-path sinuosity regression after scheduler/kselector heuristic update
text:
Contain and remediate inference-path sinuosity regression after scheduler/kselector heuristic update

description:
Summary: After merging kselector heuristic change in runtime-1.47, we observed a statistically significant increase in per-request kernel-switching (path sinuosity) for long-context streaming workloads. This led to increased p95 and p99 latency for a subset of customer requests and increased GPU kernel churn, raising overall token cost and some ECS autoscaling thrash. The regression appears correlated with the scheduler's sampling window reduction and a new kernel-ranking score that favored lower-memory negative cache candidates during probe windows.

reproduction_steps:
Deploy runtime-1.47 with kselector-heuristic v2 in a canary pool (g4dn-like hardware).
Replay synthetic trace: mix of 16-64k request-lengths with streaming enabled and intermittent bursts at 80 qps across 200 parallel clients (use replay harness: infra/replays/sinuosity/long_stream_2025.tar.gz).
Collect per-request execution path logs: /metrics/runtime/kselector/exec_path_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count.
Observe >2x increase in median kernel_switch_count and 15-40% regressed p95 latency for affected model-family (llama2-70b-quant).
Validate anomaly persists when scheduler sampling_window decreased from 250ms -> 50ms and kselector ranking uses 'prefers_low_rss' feature flag=true.

timeline:
2025-11-05: Customer report via SE: increased tail latency for streaming summarization endpoint.
2025-11-06: Oncall + runtime team confirmed latency delta; activated high-fidelity tracing and enabled verbose kselector logs on canary.
2025-11-07: Correlated with runtime-1.47 deployment and kselector heuristic rollout; reverted heuristic in one canary cluster -> immediate improvement.
2025-11-09: Reproduced locally with replay harness; created this follow-up ticket to contain and remediate.
2025-11-12: Short-term mitigation (rolled gating flag to false in all clusters) implemented; monitoring shows baseline restored but no root-cause fix yet.
2025-11-15: Began targeted profiling and kernel-level counters collection; preliminary data points collected for 1000 requests across model variants.

root_cause:
Two interacting changes produced unintended kernel-route oscillation: 1) scheduler sampling_window reduction increased the frequency of path re-evaluation under bursty load; 2) the new kselector ranking introduced a bias towards low-RSS kernels that produced marginally cheaper first-choice paths but higher incompatibility with streaming KV cache warmups, causing frequent re-routes and failed fusion opportunities. The combined effect amplified kernel-switching for long-context streaming requests, increasing tail latency and GPU context churn.

mitigations_done:
Rolled back kselector ranking change behind feature-flag across all canaries and production clusters (2025-11-12).
Increased scheduler sampling_window from 50ms back to 200ms in burst-sensitive pools to dampen re-evaluation frequency.
Enabled an emergency circuit-breaker: if kernel_switch_count > threshold for a request, pin to last-successful kernel path for remainder of request to avoid oscillation.
Notified affected customers and provided guidance for temporary rate shaping for high-concurrency streaming flows.

action_items:
(A1) Rework kselector scoring function: add compatibility term that estimates KV-cache warmup affinity (owner: Rahul Singh, due: 2025-11-20).
(A2) Implement simulation harness in CI that measures kernel_switch_count and fusion_loss_rate for representative long-context traces and surface regression alerts on PRs touching kselector or scheduler (owner: Asha Patel, estimate 3).
(A3) Add explicit canary gating for sampling_window changes with traffic-shaped experiments simulating bursty streaming (owner: SRE team, contact: Maria Chen, due: 2025-11-22).
(A4) Harden the emergency circuit-breaker logic to be configurable per-model-family and add observability for every circuit activation (owner: runtime-observability, due: 2025-11-19).
(A5) Create load-profiled benchmarks for embeddings vs. streaming workloads and run weekly acceptance tests against pre-release kernels (owner: Perf Eng, estimate 2).
(A6) Postmortem doc + retro write-up and team presentation (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2025-11-21).

notes:
We observed this primarily on model families with large KV cache footprints and streaming enabled; short-context batched workloads were largely unaffected.
Quantized kernels tended to 'lose' fusion opportunities more often due to micro-batching alignment differences — include quantization matrix in later experiments.
Security review not required for changes; performance-only surface.
